By BOA-Buildtech engineering team • Last updated 21 September 2026

Is free house or building demolition real?

It can be real in some cases — when the resale value of old timber, steel frames, or metal roofing fully offsets labor, equipment, and debris hauling. That is common for old wooden houses or steel-frame buildings. Concrete houses yield little scrap, so a fee is usual.

Watch for “free” quotations with no numbers — owners never learn what their materials are worth, and hauling or permit fees may appear later. BOA-Buildtech therefore shows demolition cost, hauling, and scrap credits as separate quotation lines.

5 factors that change demolition price the most

  1. Size and structure — reinforced concrete needs more equipment and time than timber
  2. Soi width and access — sois that backhoes or 10-wheel trucks cannot enter need manual strip-out and many small-truck trips
  3. Party walls with neighbors — require shoring and staged demolition
  4. Debris volume and haul distance to the tip — a large cost often hidden in lump-sum quotes
  5. Resale value of scrap — old timber and steel can credit against demolition cost

Does building demolition require a permit?

Yes — apply or notify the local authority first if the building meets either condition under Section 22 of the Building Control Act B.E. 2522 (1979):

  • Buildings over 15 meters high that sit within less than their own height of another building or public land
  • Buildings within less than 2 meters of another building or public land

In practice, attached row houses and townhouses, and homes tight to roads or neighbor fences, usually meet condition 2 — so file at the Bangkok district office or the municipality/Subdistrict Administrative Organization engineering division. Allow about 1–1.5 months; many local citizen guides set a ~45-day review period.

BOA-Buildtech helps prepare documents and the demolition plan for permit filing.

Note: Local rules vary. This is general guidance, not legal advice.

How many days do BOA-Buildtech demolition steps take?

Single-storey detached houses typically take about 3–7 days for demolition and hauling; two-storey about 7–14 days. Row houses may take longer due to party-wall shoring. None of this includes permit processing time.

Copper is worth far more per kilo than aluminium, so the same size can differ by nearly 2×. Check the U-bend tubes at the end of the outdoor coil: orange-red is copper, silver is aluminium. 66.content_en:
By BOA-Buildtech team • Reviewed by Mr. Songwut Saidee, Civil Engineering Fellow, PE No. 55103 • Last updated September 22, 2026

Steel pile is a prefabricated foundation made from steel pipes, with helical wings around the body, and galvanized to prevent rust. It is installed by screwing into the ground without the need for driving, so it can replace concrete piles in extension work and light structure projects. BOA-Buildtech summarizes the price and load-bearing capacity on this page from documents of the Thai Innovation Accounting of the Budget Bureau and test results according to ASTM standards, to allow homeowners and factory owners in Pathum Thani and Nonthaburi to make decisions based on real information. The overall pile system is on page pile and foundation

What is a steel pile and how many types are there?

The steel piles used in Thailand are mainly divided into two groups: screw/helical piles and micropiles that use steel pipes as the core. Both types work differently and are suitable for different applications.

steel pile screw (Screw Pile / Helical Pile)

An example of a specification registered with a government agency is a steel pile with helical wings all around, hot-dip galvanized with a thickness of at least 100 micrometers, and designed to replace concrete pile foundations. This product was developed in collaboration with King Mongkut's University of Technology North Bangkok and Chiang Mai University, and was listed in the Thai Innovation Registry for the period of August 2020 – August 2028.

In the market, there are several models according to the type of pole head, such as the FS model, which is medium-sized, withstands pushing and pulling forces better, and is suitable for houses or knockdown buildings no higher than 2 stories, for streetlight poles and CCTV poles.

steel pilemicropile (Steel-cased Micropile)

In international engineering, a micropile is a bored pile that is then filled with grout, generally with a diameter not exceeding 12 inches (approximately 300 mm), and is usually reinforced with steel. The reinforcement may be a single steel bar, multiple bars, and/or a steel casing. The most commonly used type is a single steel bar paired with a steel casing. This is therefore considered a "steel pile micropile" in engineering terms.

This meaning is different from the 'pilemicropile' that Thai people are familiar with, which is a hollow spun concrete column with steel inside, 1.5 meters long per section, joined in length by electric welding, and driven with a special crane. Read more on the page. micropile

How much is a steel pile with a screw?

The price verifiable from official sources is the Thai Innovation Account of the Budget Bureau, which specifies the price per pile at approximately 6,100–85,000 baht each, depending on size and length. These prices include VAT, but do not include shipping and installation costs.

Source: Budget Bureau, Innovation Code 01010042 — This is a public reference price, not the installation price of BOA-Buildtech

The market price for general customers has much cheaper smaller models, such as KEMREX Lite, which the manufacturer promotes at 1,999 baht per unit for extension work for floors, garages, and balconies. This promotional price can change at any time, so you should request the latest quotation every time.

Factors that cause the total price to differ: Pipe size and length, number of units as designed by the engineer, transportation and installation costs (the prices in the table do not include these two), difficulty of accessing the site, and the necessity to test load capacity

The installation price from BOA-Buildtech will be confirmed after an on-site survey and issuing a quotation with itemized details from the actual BOQ. Send on-site photos via LINE or call 061-743-9900.

How many tons can a steel pile support?

According to the test results submitted to the Budget Bureau, a 2-meter-long steel pile can withstand a compressive force at the failure point of approximately 7.4–14.7 tons, while the larger 6-meter model can handle about 80 tons. The actual design value must be divided by the safety factor determined by engineers, so it is much lower than these values.

Table: Ultimate load capacity (Qu) of KEMREX FS steel pile

modelPressure (ton)Tensile force (tons)Lateral force (tons)Test area
FS68 × 2 m.7.443.492.85Chachoengsao
FS140 × 2 m.14.667.895.59Chachoengsao
FS220 × 4 m.60248Ubon Ratchathani, Sukhothai
FS355 × 6 m.8039.379.91Lopburi

Test results reference standards ASTM D1143, ASTM D3689, and ASTM D3966, calculated using Chin's Method and represent the ultimate value

How to read numbers correctly:

  1. The values in the table are not the actual usable weights. For the 2-meter long model, the designing engineer set the Safety Factor between 2.5–4 depending on the soil layer and the structure's weight. For example, the FS68 model (Qu 7.44 tons) divided by 2.5–4 would result in a working load of approximately 1.9–3.0 tons per unit.
  2. Value changes according to the soil The document states that the Qu value can vary depending on the cohesion (C) of the soil particles, and the 2-meter model test was conducted in Chachoengsao, not Pathum Thani or Nonthaburi.
  3. Inspect during installation using torque International standards use this method to control the quality of screw piles by evaluating the load-bearing capacity in both compression and tension from the final installation torque, using a factor called Kt. For example, ICC-ES AC358 specifies an initial Kt value of 9 ft⁻¹ for 2.875-inch OD round pipes and 7 ft⁻¹ for 3.5-inch OD pipes. However, research from 799 tests found that the Kt values according to AC358 underestimate the capacity at low torque and overestimate it at high torque. For certainty, on-site load testing is recommended.

How is a steel pile micropile different from a concrete micropile?

These two types differ in the installation method and load-bearing mechanism. Steel micropiles use a drilling and grout injection method, while concrete micropiles, which are popular in Thailand, use a method of driving or pressing precast concrete piles segment by segment.

Topicsteel screw pilemicropile steel casingmicropile concrete (I / spun)
Installation methodSpin into the groundDrill, insert steel, pour cement slurryHammer or press each piece, then connect them
Weight-bearing mechanismSupport bracket at the helical wingThe friction between lime water and soil generally does not include the bearing force at the tip.Friction force and bearing force at the tip
Referable number7.4–80 tons (Qu according to the table above)Depends on the design of each projectI22 The provider stated that it can handle 18–20 tons per plant

Additional information: Micropiles are usually designed in small groups, with each pile bearing equal weight, and they are designed to withstand compressive, tensile, and lateral forces together.

Are steel piles good? Advantages and limitations you need to know

Steel piles are a good option when space is tight, fast work is required, and noise and vibrations need to be reduced. However, they are not suitable for every site because they require an engineering design and there are limitations regarding hard soil layers or rock.

Advantage

  • Minimal impact on neighbors Official documents state that it helps reduce noise, dust, and vibrations during installation
  • Install quickly The U.S. Forest Service recorded the case where 12 screw piles were installed for 4 observation platforms in 4 hours.
  • A little dirt, please Suitable for wet or soft soil areas and cost-effective in wetlands with soft clay soil

Does a steel pile rust? How many years can it last?

Steel embedded in undisturbed native soil corrodes very slowly. The main risk is in the fill soil near the ground surface. Studies by the National Bureau of Standards (now NIST) examined steel piles removed after being embedded in soil for 7–40 years and found no significant corrosion in the portions of the piles that were in native soil below the groundwater level.

For fill soil, data from literature reviews found that the corrosion rate of piles in fill soil is about twice that of undisturbed natural soil. Therefore, if there is information on the electrochemical properties of the soil, engineers can design for the loss of steel or zinc over the service life. And if there is no data, a conservative corrosion rate assumption will be used first.

As for the figures provided by the manufacturer, the zinc coating layer is more than 100 microns thick, and according to tests, it corrodes on average about 1 micron per year. This number comes from the manufacturer, not independent research.

ข้อจำกัด

  • A specialist must determine the size and measure the soil, and a specialized hydraulic driver must be used.
  • Not suitable for soil with a lot of rocks or areas where the rock layer is close to the surface, and not designed to drill through hard rock layers.
  • Debris or stones in the fill soil can be an obstacle. In one case study, the installation encountered a large stone, which prevented the pile from being driven and caused it to deviate in position, requiring the pile to be removed and the installation point to be relocated.
  • Precautions regarding lateral thrust: From the table above, the lateral force for the 2-meter model is approximately 2.9–5.6 tons, which is lower than the compressive force. Work subjected to wind or soil pressure, such as signs or walls, must be separately reviewed by an engineer.

Can steel piles be used with soft soil in Pathum Thani–Nonthaburi?

Usable for light constructions as calculated by engineers, but it must be understood that the lower central region has thick soft clay layers, so short piles mainly bear weight through soft soil. Research on Bangkok soil layers indicates there is soft to medium clay 13–16 meters thick, followed by hard clay layers reaching about 21–28 meters, and the soft clay has high natural moisture content, with an average undrained shear strength of only 10–20 kN/m².

In practice, it means:

  • 2-meter steel pile suitable for light-weight work such as carports, balconies, or extension floors, as calculated by an engineer to be able to support.
  • For projects that need to reduce differential settlement between the extension and the existing house, an engineer should compare them with longer piles.
  • A civil engineer should analyze and select the type of pile from the soil investigation drilling report.

How to choose a steel needle company to get standard-quality work?

A good steel pile company should have engineers who design based on actual soil data, use piles with specified galvanized coatings and test results, record torque for each pile, and separate the prices for the piles, transportation, and installation so they can be verified, rather than just offering the lowest price per pile.

Checklist before hiring a steel nail company

Things to askWhy is it important?
Is there a civil engineer designing and using data from soil investigation drilling?The selection of pile type should be based on the soil investigation report, and the allowable load varies according to soil properties.
How thick is a hot-dip galvanized pile?The specifications registered with the government agency specify at least 100 micrometers.
Which standard does the load test comply with?Sample registered referencing ASTM D1143, D3689, and D3966
Record the final torque of every tree or not?Installation torque is used to assess and control the load-bearing capacity of screw piles.
Can the weight be tested on-site?Torque-based estimates can be inaccurate, both underestimating and overestimating, and tests on piles, such as Load Tests, help increase confidence.
Do you have product liability insurance?Some products indicate that they have Product Liability Insurance according to the manufacturer's terms.
Does the quotation separate transportation and installation costs?The government reference price is the pile price excluding transportation and installation costs.

"Khem Hlek Co., Ltd." is who? It is the name of a company that manufactures and registers Thai innovations of steel piles under the brand KEMREX, and the documents from the Budget Bureau list dozens of distributors. Choose the wall type from retained height and setback

The system is not chosen from the cheapest price, but from the soil height to retain, space available for the footing, and distance from neighboring property lines.

Cantilever

The standard type for typical plots. The footing projects inward to counter the moment. Suitable for retained heights up to 3.0 m when there is room for the projecting footing.

Counterfort

Adds rear counterfort ribs at intervals, reducing wall stem thickness when soil is high. Suitable for retained heights of 3.0–4.0 m and long continuous runs.

Sheet pile wall

Used when there is no room for a projecting footing, or soil must be retained tight to the property line. Requires the least setback of the three types.

6 steps for retaining wall works

  1. Survey levels and boundaries — measure retained height, setbacks from property lines, and surface water flow direction
  2. Structural design — set wall type, footing size, and reinforcement from actual earth pressure
  3. Piles and foundation — bore piles to drawing positions, cut pile heads, pour lean concrete, and tie footing steel
  4. Pre-pour inspection — engineer checks bar spacing, cover, formwork, and bracing; the owner always signs off before pour
  5. Concrete pour and curing — pour in stages at defined joints, take cubes for testing, and cure per specification
  6. Drainage and backfill — install drainage pipes and filter stone behind the wall, compact backfill in 30 cm layers, and hand over the full document pack

Factors that change retaining wall price

These four factors drive steel, concrete, and pile quantities — the main cost of wall works.

  • Retained soil height — earth pressure rises faster than height; doubling height does not simply double the steel
  • Soil strata and pile type — soft soils need longer piles or a different pile system
  • Site access — if mixers and machines cannot reach, pumping or extra handling is required
  • Surcharge on soil behind the wall — roads, parking, or buildings behind the wall must be included from the design stage

What types of work does our aluminum glass door and window installation service cover?

We offer installation of aluminum glass doors and windows for new homes, replacement of old deteriorated units, and renovations that require modifying the size of openings. Our services range from single bathroom doors to entire buildings with dozens of units. We manufacture frames and assemble the doors according to the actual measurements on site, not using prefabricated doors that have to be forced to fit the openings.

Aluminum door

Sliding doors (2-panel / 4-panel / hanging track), single-double swing doors, folding bi-fold doors, frameless tempered glass doors for shops and offices, equipped with locks, handles, and door closers according to usage — for storefronts that open and close hundreds of times a day, we recommend upgrading to heavy-duty hardware from the start, as replacing door closers later is more expensive than the price difference at installation.

Aluminum window

Sliding windows with 2–4 panels, awning windows, adjustable louver windows, fixed windows (non-opening, for light only), and sliding windows with top light panels. Frame colors can be chosen from white baked, tea, black, anodized, and wood grain. Installed together with mosquito screens or security bars in a single job.

Replacement work and opening repair work

Dismantle the old wooden or steel frames that are decayed and replace them with aluminum, including work that requires breaking to expand or reduce the opening, applying new sealant around the frame, and finishing the plaster neatly. This part is usually not accepted by general glass shops because it requires a plaster worker as well.

How is the installation price of aluminum glass per square meter calculated, and how much does it start from?

The installation price of aluminum glass doors and windows in the 2026 market is approximately 2,400–12,500 THB per square meter, depending on the type of panel, the thickness of the aluminum frame, and the type of glass. Installation labor is usually charged separately at about 800–1,500 THB per square meter. Our price is quoted as a total per set of panels after on-site measurement, with no additional costs during the work if the scope of work does not change.

Things to know before comparing price per square meter: Aluminum craftsmen do not actually calculate costs by square meter. The main costs are aluminum sections according to the perimeter length, glass according to the area, and fittings according to the number of sets. As a result, smaller panels always have a higher price per square meter than larger panels. A 60×60 cm bathroom window may cost 6,000 baht per square meter, while a large sliding panel of 2.4×1.1 meters costs only 2,800 baht per square meter, even though the materials are the same set. Therefore, the price per square meter can only be used as a preliminary check to see if the quotation is reasonable, and should not be used to decide whether to hire the work.

4 factors that cause price movement: Aluminum profile thickness · Type and thickness of glass · Grade of lock-wheel-shock equipment · Height and difficulty of access to the site (3rd floor and above or requiring scaffolding will incur additional costs)

How to choose line thickness and type of glass to suit the work

For typical residential homes, 1.5 mm thick aluminum profiles are the most cost-effective. They are strong enough for standard-sized panels and reduce frame warping issues that can lead to long-term leakage. Profiles of 1.2 mm are suitable for small panels with low stress, while 2.0 mm and above are used for extra-large panels or buildings exposed to high wind forces.

The safest way to select an aluminum glass technician is to check 3 things before placing a deposit: a quotation that specifies all the specs (thickness, type of glass, brand of equipment), warranty conditions in writing, and real work that can be verified. What does our aluminum awning installation cover?

We install all 4 aluminum awning systems. The difference between systems is not only appearance — it is how far they can project without posts, how much load the wall must carry, and how well they stop wind-driven rain. The team surveys first and recommends the suitable system — not the most expensive as a default starting point.

C-channel frame awning

“C-channel” refers to the framing section that supports the cladding — not the cladding material itself. This system can be clad with metal sheet, polycarbonate, or vinyl. It is the easiest to keep on budget and suits covering large areas such as carports or full rear yards.

Adjustable aluminum louver awning

The only one of the 4 systems with adjustable louvers — close them in driving rain and open for breeze when rain stops. Suited to townhouses or homes with narrow, stuffy rear yards where a solid roof would trap heat and block airflow. The trade-off is moving parts and gutters that need periodic sediment cleaning.

Aluminum composite awning

Aluminum composite panels (ACP) sandwich a core between aluminum skins, weighing about 3–10 kg/sq.m. by thickness and model. Suited when the awning should read as continuous with a commercial façade. Always ask whether the core is fire-retardant — especially near kitchens or neighbor property lines.

Wood-grain aluminum awning

Wood-grain coated aluminum replaces real timber to avoid repainting and termites. On awnings it is used as sun louvers or soffit cladding. Understand that wood-grain louvers have gaps between blades and do not stop rain alone — a waterproof layer must always sit above them.

How much does aluminum awning installation cost?

Installation is priced in THB per square meter, driven mainly by the system chosen, projection, and site access difficulty. Jobs under 10 sq.m. often cost more per square meter because transport and installation do not scale down with area. Price depends on the real site — free assessment and a confirmed price after a line-item quotation.

Every quotation itemizes materials, framing, labor, and removal of existing works so you can compare other contractors fairly.

How many days does aluminum awning installation take?

Typical home-size awnings take 1–3 on-site days for solid systems and 2–4 days for adjustable louvers — counting only days the crew is working. From assessment to handover is usually 7–14 days because materials are cut to measured sizes. Owners need not stay all day, but should be present for assessment and handover inspection.

  4. On-site installation — fix framing, install cladding, form gutters and outlets

Does an awning extension need a permit?

Ministerial Regulation No. 55 under building-control law requires eaves or awnings to stay at least 50 cm from the property line. Extensions from a balcony or second floor must stay at least 2 m from the line. Alterations that count as building modification need local authority approval before work starts.

In practice, district offices and municipalities interpret “building modification” differently. Our team checks setbacks on assessment day and says plainly if the desired design risks non-compliance — offering adjustments such as shorter projection or relocated gutters, instead of taking the job and leaving the owner with the problem later.

86.content_en:
How much does contracted land filling cost, and how is it priced so it does not blow out?

Land filling is priced by volume (cubic meters), not square meters. Lump-sum fill rates in Pathum Thani–Rangsit are about 240–500 THB per compacted cubic meter, depending on material, compaction level, and haul distance from the borrow pit. If a contractor quotes “THB per square meter” without stating fill thickness, or “THB per truck” without stating how many cubic meters the truck holds, that price cannot be compared fairly with others.

Loose vs compacted cubic meters — the dispute that causes the most arguments

Loose cubic meters are soil volume on the truck bed. Compacted cubic meters are the volume remaining in the plot after compaction. Soil settles about 15–25% between those stages, so 1,000 loose cubic meters become only about 750–850 cubic meters of real work.

That is why many clients feel they “paid for 100 cu.m. but only got 80” even when the contractor was not cheating — each side used a different unit from the start. BOA-Buildtech prices compacted cubic meters, measuring levels with a surveying level before work and after compaction, then calculating volume from the level difference. Clients pay for work actually delivered — no counting truck trips, no guessing whether a truck was “full.”

General fill (borrow/black soil), graded smooth240–320 THB120–160 THB240–320 THBRaise vacant land; flood protection; fill for sale
General fill + layered compaction ≥95% Standard Proctor320–420 THB160–210 THB320–420 THBPrepare for houses, buildings, warehouses

Conditions for this table — read before comparing other quotes

  • Every cell is per compacted cubic meter (volume after compaction), not loose truck-bed volume
  • “Equiv. per sq.m.” converts units at the stated thickness only — it is not a lump per-sq.m. rate
  • Excludes hauling cleared debris to disposal — priced by distance and tip fees
  • Excludes the 2,000 THB fill-notification fee when notification is required
  • Assumes haul from the borrow pit within 25 km of the site

Fair comparison method: if another contractor quotes 350 THB per loose cubic meter, that equals about 440 THB compacted (350 ÷ 0.8). Before deciding who is cheaper, ask one question: “Is this loose or compacted cubic meters?”

What land clearing before fill includes

Land clearing prepares the plot before soil arrives: cutting trees, removing weeds, clearing obstacles, and stripping 15–30 cm of organic topsoil for disposal. Every fill job should pass this step first. Filling over grass, roots, or original topsoil lets organics decay and leave voids that settle into holes later.

Clearing costs about 15–35 THB per square meter on open land, with debris hauling priced separately. Plots in Nong Suea and Lam Luk Ka that were orchard ditches or fish ponds need much more work — pumping, removing soft sludge, and backfilling ditches first. Always assess on site.

5 factors that change fill price

  1. Distance from borrow pit to site — haul cost is the main cost, not the soil itself. Two plots in the same subdistrict can differ 20–30% just from pit distance
  2. Fill material type — general fill is cheapest; laterite costs more because it is selected borrow with better engineering properties
  3. Required compaction level — smooth grading alone vs 20–30 cm layered compaction with density testing differs greatly in equipment and time
  4. Access conditions — housing-estate sois that block 10-wheel trucks force 6-wheel trucks and nearly double the trip count
  5. Existing site condition — overgrown plots with large trees, orchard ditches, fish ponds, or soft sludge all increase work quantity

How many cubic meters and days to fill 1 rai?

One rai (1,600 sq.m.) filled 1 m high needs 1,600 compacted cubic meters — about 2,000 loose cubic meters ordered, or roughly 180 ten-wheel trips. Real work time is 7–10 days. Formula: area (sq.m.) × fill thickness (m) = compacted volume, then allow about 25% more for settlement to find loose volume to order.

3 conditions that make work slower than the table

  • Rain — May to October, soil wetter than optimum moisture cannot meet density specs; work must dry or stop. Always allow rain days. A contractor who promises the same schedule in rain is not planning standard compaction
  • Inner-city truck bans — jobs into inner Bangkok have restricted truck hours and far fewer daily trips. Rangsit–Thanyaburi–Lam Luk Ka work on Rangsit–Nakhon Nayok and canal-side roads runs more continuously
  • Narrow access — if 10-wheel trucks cannot enter, 6-wheel trucks nearly double trip count and stretch the schedule

How high to fill in Rangsit, Thanyaburi, and Lam Luk Ka to stay above flood level

There is no single standard number for every plot. Correct level comes from three values together: level relative to the public road in front, highest known flood level in that soi, and allowance for future settlement. Adjacent plots in the same subdistrict can differ by 30–40 cm if they sit on different canal sides.

How to find the right fill level for your plot

  1. Measure road crown level in front as the main reference. Plots below the road always take road runoff in the rainy season
  2. Ask long-time neighbors how high water rose and in which years. The Rangsit plain relies on the Rangsit Prayurasakdi canal system and water gates, so flood history differs sharply inside vs outside flood dikes
  3. Allow for settlement by fill thickness and original strata — today’s perfect level will be lower next year
  4. Check whether fill will be higher than neighbors — if so, drainage is required and a retaining wall may be needed by law

Zone-specific caution: many Lam Luk Ka and Nong Suea plots were orchard ditches or rice paddies with thick soft sludge. Filling without removing sludge first causes abnormal settlement. We check and disclose this at survey.

Can you build a house right after filling?

It depends on what you build. Piled buildings that transfer load to stiff strata below can start as soon as compaction passes criteria — no need to wait 6–12 months, because building load is not carried by the fill.

What must wait is work sitting directly on fill — ground-bearing slabs, internal roads, concrete yards, fences, and landscaping. Wait through at least one rainy season, or if you must build now, design those as pile-supported slabs. Advice that says “always wait 6–12 months after fill” is overly blanket and wastes owners’ time.

Must land filling be notified to the local authority?

It depends on mound area. If the fill mound exceeds 2,000 sq.m. (about 1 rai 1 ngan), notify the local authority before starting under Section 26 of the Excavation and Land Filling Act B.E. 2543 (2000), and start only after receiving the acknowledgment. Areas ≤ 2,000 sq.m. need no notification but still have legal drainage duties.

Legal duties in plain language

CaseWhat you must doPenalty if violated
Fill higher than neighboring land of a different owner, mound area ≤ 2,000 sq.m.No notification, but provide adequate drainage so neighbors are not harmedFine up to 10,000 THB
Mound area > 2,000 sq.m.Notify local authority; wait for acknowledgment (issued within 7 days); then start. Acknowledgment fee 2,000 THBImprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to 50,000 THB, or both

4 things landowners often do not know

  1. Localities may set a threshold below 2,000 sq.m. The Act only caps declared areas at 2,000 sq.m. Rangsit City Municipality, Thanyaburi Town Municipality, Lam Luk Ka Town Municipality, and each Subdistrict Administrative Organization may differ — always check where the land sits
  2. An acknowledgment does not shield liability — if fill damages neighboring land or houses, owner and filler still owe compensation, and neighbors may be complainants in criminal cases
  3. Neighbors can request a stop-work order — anyone harmed or reasonably expecting harm can ask the local authority to stop filling immediately
  4. If the filler is a juristic person, directors or managers who ordered the work may also be liable — not the company alone

BOA-Buildtech checks these conditions at site survey and can file notification with the local authority for the owner when thresholds apply.

Summary based on the Excavation and Land Filling Act B.E. 2543 (2000) for basic understanding — not legal advice. Details and area thresholds may differ by local ordinance.

Will filled land settle? What do we warrant?

Straight answer: some settlement always occurs, and no contractor can warrant zero settlement. What can be controlled is fill-layer compaction quality. Settlement of soft clay below is natural to the Central Plain. Ads that say “fill with no settlement” promise something the contractor cannot control.

Settlement comes from 2 sources — only one is controllable

Settlement sourceCauseControllable?
Compression of the fill itselfInsufficient density, layers too thick, organic contamination, wrong moisture100% controllable — this is what we warrant
Consolidation of soft clay under the siteFill weight squeezes water from original strata over timeNot controllable — property of original strata

Pathum Thani and northern Bangkok have soft clay about 10–18 m thick below the surface. Filling 1 m adds roughly 1.8–2.0 tons/sq.m. of surcharge, causing settlement that may reach tens of centimeters over years. Exact amounts need plot-specific boring data — which is why building fill must plan settlement allowance from the start.

BOA-Buildtech warranty

What we warrant

  • Fill dry density not less than 95% Standard Proctor for construction-prep fill, with field density test documents on handover
  • Placed and compacted in 20–30 cm layers with a vibratory roller — not by driving an excavator over the surface
  • Billed soil volume from before/after level difference on site, with level data handed to the client
  • 2-year compaction warranty — localized settlement proven from our compaction quality is repaired free

What is excluded (stated clearly in the contract)

  • Natural settlement of original strata below, which we assess and disclose before starting
  • Damage from natural disasters, flooding, or groundwater level changes
  • Use beyond design intent — e.g. parking heavy trucks on fill prepared for light use
  • Work where the owner reduced specs — e.g. requesting no compaction or cheaper soil than proposed

Which fill soil to choose? Laterite vs general fill

Choose by what will sit on the land next — not by price alone. General fill raises level; laterite is for roads and parking. A common myth is that laterite is cheaper than general fill — it is more expensive because it is selected borrow with better grading and bearing.

MaterialBest forNot suited forWatch-outs

LateriteInternal roads, parking, site access, subbasePlanting / gardensCosts more than general fill; must be compacted to get full benefit
Crushed rockPavement layers; temporary heavy-vehicle surfacesLarge-volume level raising (unnecessarily expensive)Use as top road layers — not to fill the whole plot
Fill sandFast drainage; tight sites using pumped placementGeneral level raising (costly and flows easily)Needs edge containment; compaction moisture must be controlled

Naming note: the market often swaps “hard soil” and “laterite,” causing confusion. Both usually mean lateritic soil — dialect and pit source differ. When requesting quotes, ask for property values such as CBR or required density so everyone discusses the same thing.

Laterite fill for internal roads and parking

Laterite suits vehicle loads — project roads, parking, construction access, and pavement subbase — because particle grading compacts to high density and drains better than general fill, which holds water and softens in rain.

Laterite fill costs about 380–500 THB per compacted cubic meter — higher than general fill as selected borrow. Two watch-outs: (1) laterite only performs if truly compacted — dumping and grading alone becomes potholes in the first rains; (2) do not laterite-fill an entire plot if you plan to plant trees — roots struggle to penetrate.

Two myths that ruin fill jobs from the start

Myth 1: “I want to plant trees, so fill the whole plot with loam.”
Good structural fill must be inorganic, free of roots and plant debris — organics decay and leave voids that settle later. Correct method: fill and compact with structural soil to full level first, then cover with 20–30 cm topsoil only where gardens go.

Myth 2: “Compact the fill well and you don’t need piles.”
Buildings in this area always transfer load to piles — not to the fill. Good fill and compaction keep ground-bearing slabs, internal roads, fences, and landscaping from settling apart from the building — they do not replace piled foundations. A contractor who says compacted fill removes the need for piles is a red flag — walk away.

7 steps of land filling work

  1. Site survey and leveling — measure existing levels vs the public road, check boundary markers, access, and neighbors. Free of charge
  2. Calculate soil volume and issue a line-item quotation — state compacted volume needed, target level, material, compaction level, and whether local notification is required
  3. Prepare the site — cut trees, clear weeds, strip 15–30 cm organic topsoil, and haul away before filling
  4. Protect neighbors and set temporary drainage — form temporary berms and ditches before soil arrives — both a legal duty and the most common neighbor dispute cause
  5. Haul soil and compact in layers — place 20–30 cm layers, control moisture near optimum, compact with a vibratory roller to full level
  6. Field density tests and closing levels — record density in specified layers and measure post-compaction levels to bill real compacted volume
  7. Final grading and handover — grade for drainage, clean the public road, hand over with density tests, level data, and acknowledgment (if any)

Follow-on services in one team — BOA’s advantage

Filled land usually needs more work next. As a full construction contractor, BOA-Buildtech plans ahead during fill — far cheaper than tearing out later.

What does BOA-Buildtech's solar cell installation service cover?

We provide a complete service all in one, from roof inspection, system design, installation, submitting documents for electricity authority approval, to after-sales service by a professional team.

Install on-grid solar cell systems with a capacity of 3–20 kW

The system connects to the power grid, using electricity from the panels directly during the day without a battery. It has the lowest cost and the fastest payback. It supports both 1-phase homes and 3-phase buildings, from 3 kW to 20 kW.

Install hybrid solar cells system with 10 kWh battery

Store excess energy for use at night and during power outages. Suitable for homes that use a lot of electricity at night or areas with frequent power cuts. Which type of home solar cells is better: On-Grid or Hybrid?

For homes that use a lot of electricity during the day and already have electricity from the power company, an On-Grid system is the most cost-effective because it does not have the cost of batteries, which are the most expensive component of the system. As for 1 Phase or 3 Phase, refer to the existing electrical system of the house. If the meter is 1 phase (most typical homes), use a 1 Phase system. 88.content_en:
By BOA-Buildtech Civil Team • Updated 21 September 2026

Row-house and townhouse demolition differs from tearing down a detached house in the middle of a plot because of party walls, narrow sois, and neighbors still living next door. This page focuses on that group. Overall demolition costs, permits, and steps are on the house demolition services page.

How row house / townhouse demolition differs from a detached house

Detached homes with enough setback can often be knocked with a backhoe and hauled. Row houses and townhouses must be stripped in stages, shore walls against neighbors, and control dust, noise, and debris from entering neighboring openings. If a contractor quotes cheap because they will “knock the whole building in one day” without mentioning shoring, treat it as not having assessed neighbor risk.

How we handle party walls so neighbors do not crack

  • Photo-record neighboring walls, floors, and ceilings before work starts
  • Shore or strengthen the party wall per frame condition — never hit the party wall first
  • Strip from the roof and projecting parts first, then work down
  • Dust-control at openings and shared soi walkways

If new cracks are proven from our demolition, BOA-Buildtech inspects and repairs under contract — we do not push liability onto the neighbor.

End units vs mid-terrace — is difficulty different?

Clearly yes. End or corner units have a party wall on one side and open access on the other for machines. Mid-terrace units have party walls on both sides — shore both sides and strip only from front/back. Work is slower and price per square meter sits at the top of the range. Demolishing several adjoining units together means our own party walls between units need no shoring, lowering cost per unit.

After demolition, who cares for the newly exposed neighbor wall?

Agree this clearly before starting. A party wall that was once sheltered will face sun and rain for the first time. Without finishing, seepage often appears on the neighbor side within one rainy season and becomes a dispute. BOA-Buildtech lists wall finishing as a separate quotation line — plaster and waterproofing or cladding — and informs the neighbor of the method before work.

How much does row-house demolition cost?

About 350–800 THB per square meter for residential work. Permit fees are a separate line. Hauling is included for tips at normal distance. Three factors push price up: storeys, party-wall length to shore, and sois that large trucks cannot enter.

Site conditionEffect on price and time
End / corner unit; backhoe accessFaster; lower range (~350 THB/sq.m.)
Mid-terrace; party walls both sidesShore both sides; price rises
Narrow soi; small machines / manual laborMore work days; upper range (~800 THB/sq.m.)
2+ storeysStaged strip-out — never push the whole building over at once
Several adjoining unitsInter-unit walls need no shoring; cost per unit drops

Ranges from jobs BOA-Buildtech has completed. Confirmed only in the post-survey quotation. Do not compare with “from 150 THB/sq.m.” signs that omit hauling, shoring, and permits.

Can row-house demolition be free?

Usually not — row houses are mostly concrete, and recovered steel rarely covers labor, shoring, and hauling out of a soi. What we value and credit as visible lines are structural rebar, steel roller doors, window bars, and metal roofing. If someone offers “free row-house demolition,” ask whether party-wall shoring, hauling, and neighbor liability are included.

Does row-house demolition need a permit?

Almost every unit does, because it sits within 2 m of another building or public land under Building Control Act Section 22. Buildings over 15 m within less than their height of others also qualify. Local authorities have 45 days to decide and may extend twice more by 45 days each — file at least 1–2 months before the desired start.

We check at survey and can file Form Khor.1 for the owner in our service districts. When approved you receive Permit Form A.1. Government fees are a separate quotation line — not buried silently in a lump sum.

After demolition, if you are not rebuilding on the same land, the owner must notify the registrar and return the house registration.

Legal summary above is for basic understanding — confirm with the local authority for that property before starting.

If the soi is too narrow for machines, can we still demolish?

Yes, but the method changes. Backhoes sized for detached homes often cannot enter row-house sois. Work uses smaller machines, more manual strip-out, and many 6-wheel haul trips. Price per square meter and days are higher than jobs with large-machine access.

Send photos of the entrance, soi width, and turning space at assessment. We say early how far we can reach — not on the start day.

How many days do BOA-Buildtech row-house steps take?

On-site work for one unit typically takes several days to about two weeks, excluding up to 45 days waiting for the permit. Mid-terrace and narrow sois take longer.

Why row-house jobs should not go to the cheapest teardown quote

The first costs cut are always shoring, neighbor condition records, and clearing debris on the last day — resulting in cracked neighbors, dirty sois, and owners hiring someone else to clear rubble piles. Owners of old wooden houses often search for wooden-house demolition and buying old timber at the same time. The real need is someone to demolish the house and credit reusable timber against the cost. This page covers wooden-house demolition in Pathum Thani, Rangsit, Thanyaburi, and Lam Luk Ka specifically. The overall house demolition overview is at house demolition services.

Timber salvage vs full tear-down — what’s the difference?

MethodBest whenTrade-off

Choose the method from the actual frame condition — not from advertising claims. BOA-Buildtech tells you at survey how much timber can be salvaged and lists the credit as a quotation line.

Do you buy old timber? How much credit against demolition?

We do not run a separate timber-buying shop. What we can do is credit timber and scrap steel against demolition and disposal cost by species, length, and condition on the day of work. Teak and redwood that are still straight credit more than rubberwood or heavily painted timber. Termite-hollowed wood usually credits nothing.

“Free wooden-house demolition — we buy timber on site” ads are real for some high-value timber houses, but often trade away hauling, permits, or leaving the job once timber is removed. Market-wide free-demolition conditions are on the house demolition services FAQ section.

Wooden houses with asbestos tiles or old roofs — how we demolish

Asbestos cement roof sheets must not be smashed into timber debris. Wet them, remove as sheets, and haul to a facility that accepts this material. Handling is priced separately. Tell us at survey if you see brittle grey corrugated cement sheets.

Electrical systems and meters in old wooden houses are often still live — cancel the meter before demolition, same as masonry houses. Never demolish while circuits are energized.

Single-storey wooden houses roughly 15,000–80,000 THB per building before scrap credit. Two-storey or timber–masonry mixes cost more. Typical size takes 3–7 business days including hauling.

  1. Survey timber species, termites, roof, and haul routes
  2. Agree salvage vs tear-down and estimate credits
  3. Cancel meter, cordon the area, and separate asbestos sheets if present
  4. Demolish by the agreed method; separate timber, steel, and waste
  5. Haul clear and hand over the site

If the house mixes timber with a row-house masonry section, the masonry against neighbors uses the same method as row house and townhouse demolition — not mixed with timber salvage.

By BOA-Buildtech Civil Team (BOA and partners) • Updated 13 September 2026

Interior demolition is not tearing down the whole house — it removes parts that block renovation, such as partitions, old bathrooms, masonry kitchens, and finishes no longer needed. This page covers that scope. Whole-house demolition is at house demolition services.

Which walls can be knocked out, and which must not?

Wall typeCan knock out?What to check
Partition — clay brick / block, not supporting beamsYesElectrical and plumbing runs in the wall
Lightweight — gypsum, steel studYesCeiling fixings and services in the cavity

BOA-Buildtech will not accept jobs where the client orders load-bearing walls removed without a strengthening plan. If opening a ceiling reveals a load-bearing wall, we stop and present options — we do not continue just to finish on schedule.

Bathroom and kitchen strip-out — can you stay in the house?

Yes outside the rooms being stripped, but expect dust, noise, and water cut-offs in that zone. Bathroom strip-outs often leave tile and mortar stuck to pipes — plan a backup bathroom. Homes with young children, elderly residents, or people working from home should limit noisy hours in the contract.

  • Close other doors with plastic sheeting to keep dust out of living zones
  • Move fragile items away from walls to be knocked out
  • Isolate water/power only on related circuits — do not cut the whole house unless necessary

How much does interior demolition cost?

About 200–500 THB per square meter for wall knock-out and surface strip-out that does not touch structure. Debris hauling is priced per truck trip separately. Beam strengthening, relocating main plumbing, or breaking thick concrete slabs are quoted as separate lines.

Do not compare interior per-sq.m. rates with whole-house demolition. Debris volume is lower, but care for the structure and people still living there is higher.

Is a permit required for interior demolition?

Work that only removes partitions, finishes, and sanitary fixtures without touching building structure usually falls outside whole-building demolition under Section 22. Changing room layouts, relocating bathrooms, or cutting new openings may count as building alteration that needs local notice. Districts interpret differently — we tell you at survey whether thresholds apply.

  1. Walk walls, openings, and suspected structural points
  2. Define rooms to strip, rooms still livable, and noisy-hour windows
  3. Isolate systems at point, dust-control, move belongings
  4. Knock out and strip in sequence; clear debris daily so walkways stay open
  5. Post-demolition site clearing for material leaving the house, then hand over to renovation trades

The cheapest house demolition quotes in the market often cut debris hauling. When the teardown finishes, a pile of rubble remains and the owner must find someone to clear it. This page is post-demolition site clearing that should sit in the same contract as house demolition services — not a leftover separate job at the end.

What post-demolition site clearing includes

  • Haul concrete, brick, timber, and construction waste to approved disposal points
  • Separate scrap steel for credit if listed in the quotation
  • Keep debris clear of property lines and public ways
  • Rough-grade so the next trade’s vehicles can access

This is not yet layered fill and leveling with compaction. Raising level or preparing for a building needs separate level survey and compaction. We can continue with the same team.

How debris hauling is priced (by area)

Priced by area (THB/sq.m.) from debris volume and distance to the tip — not the same as a simple per-trip transport job. A single-storey detached house and a two-storey row house differ clearly in volume — we survey and itemize in the quotation. TODO: confirm price range

Dumping debris roadside, on vacant land, or into canals is illegal. Tip fees are a real cost — not a line to cut so the quote looks cheap.

After grading, what can follow?

When the site is clear and levels are workable, next works BOA-Buildtech can continue in the same contract are:

  • Fill and leveling to raise above flood level or prepare for building
  • Retaining walls if fill will be higher than neighboring land
  • New fences and boundary lines
  • Piles and foundations for a new house
  • Electrical systems and continuing structure works

This is where demolition-only companies cannot continue — and why you should hire a construction contractor who demolishes and continues, not the cheapest teardown crew followed by a full re-coordination.

Site clearing steps

What is clearing land, and how is it different from leveling land and fill soil?

clearing land (Land Clearing) is the removal of all obstacles on the land surface, such as grass, weeds, trees, stumps, trash, and construction debris, leaving bare soil where the boundaries and actual levels of the land can be seen. It is the very first step in land preparation beforefill soil Leveling or starting construction

Many landowners refer to all three tasks together as 'clearing the land,' but in the quotation, they are listed separately, with different prices and machinery. This table helps to make it clearer.

Clearing and leveling the area It is the combination of the first two jobs into a single hire. Suitable for plots where the original ground level is still usable, requiring no additional filling. Helps save the cost of one round of machinery transport.

What does BOA-Buildtech's clearing work cover?

The team takes on jobs ranging from small house plots to several rai of land. The work is divided into 4 groups, and you can choose to hire for only some parts or for all.

Clear the grass and clear the wasteland

Cut tall grass, shrubs, and weeds that have grown to cover the area. Suitable for land that has been left for many years until the boundaries are no longer visible, or before scheduling a survey officer.

Cut down trees and dig up stumps

Cut down unwanted trees, then use an excavator to remove the stumps and main roots. After that, fill the stump holes to level them. For trees that the owner wants to keep, the team will mark them before starting work every time.

Dismantle debris and carry it out of the area

Collect garbage, concrete debris, wood debris, and small structures such as old sheds or fences, pile them up, and transport them out by truck, charged according to the actual number of truck trips.

Clearing work with ground leveling (grading and compaction)

After clearing, level the soil evenly, smooth it to allow water to flow in the correct direction, and compact the spots that were previously pits to prevent them from sinking into depressions later.

How much does the land clearing work cost?

The price for land clearing work does not have a single figure that applies to every plot, as it is calculated based on the land size, the density of plants and trees, the amount of debris to be removed, and the accessibility for machinery. BOA-Buildtech therefore provides the price after reviewing photos or surveying the site, breaking it down into items according to the table below.

Factors that cause prices to rise or fall

  1. Land size — Large-scale farms usually have a lower average cost per rai, because the machinery costs are distributed over many rai.
  2. Density and size of trees — Just grass takes much less time than perennial trees, which require digging up the stumps multiple times.
  3. The amount of debris that needs to be removed — The more concrete debris or trash there is, the more trips the truck has to make.
  4. Machine entrance — Narrow alley, dirt road, or having to transport through the village may require using small machinery which works slower
  5. Soil conditions and seasons — Water-saturated clay during the rainy season slows down work and risks vehicles getting stuck

How to compare quotations without getting additional charges later

Before signing a contract, ask every contractor the same set of questions: Does the price include hauling debris off-site or just piling it up, will stumps be dug out or cut flush with the ground, will the holes from the stumps be filled, and does the price include moving the equipment? The two quotes that differ significantly usually differ on these four points.

How is the site clearing process carried out and how many days does it take?

The clearing work at the BOA-Buildtech site has 6 steps, from receiving information to handover. Plots no larger than 1 rai that only have grass and shrubs usually finish in 1–2 working days. As for plots with large trees, stumps, or many construction debris, it may take 3–7 days or more.

  1. Receive preliminary information — The owner sends the location coordinates, size according to the title deed, and photos or videos of the site via LINE for a rough price estimate.
  2. สำรวจหน้างาน — Walk along the boundary and locate the deed markers, inspect the machinery access points, electrical wires, pipes, ditches, and mark the trees that need to be preserved
  3. Send a quotation with separate items + work plan — Specify the start date, number of days, machinery used, and what is included/excluded in the price
  4. Clear in order — Cut down large trees first, followed by clearing plants, dig out the stumps, and then pile the debris in one spot
  5. Remove debris and clean up the work — Remove debris from the area, fill stump holes, and level the surface (if hiring clearing/land leveling work)
  6. Delivered with before-and-after photos — Walk through the work inspection with the owner and take comparison photos to keep as evidence

Key points that we emphasize at every event: Mark the boundary clearly before the machinery goes in Because overgrown land often hides the boundary lines, encroaching on neighboring land is the most common cause of disputes in this type of work.

What should be careful about before clearing land in Pathum Thani–Nonthaburi?

Land in the Rangsit, Lam Luk Ka, Khlong Luang, Thanyaburi, and Bang Bua Thong zones is mostly soft clay that holds water, and many plots were previously orchards or old rice fields. Clearing in this area therefore needs to plan for water management and subsidence at the same time, not just clearing the land.

  • An old garden furrow covered with grass so that it cannot be seen — This is a spot where backhoe trucks often get stuck. You should always walk around to check the trench lines first.
  • Rainy season around May–October — The soil is muddy, making it difficult for vehicles to enter, and the wheels damage the surface soil. Many plots should be scheduled for work during the dry season.
  • Unfilled potholes and compaction — It will become a sinkhole under the house floor or the parking lot in a few years
  • Village entrance and narrow alley — Housing estates must obtain permission from the legal entity first, and some dirt roads cannot support the full weight of trucks.
  • Ditches and public drainage channels beside the plots — Must prevent soil and wood debris from being pushed down to block the waterway

When should you hire for clearing the area?

Clearing the area should be hired immediately when there is a plan to use the land, or when the overgrowth begins to create risks and costs. Common situations include

  • Before building a house, warehouse, or factory — The contractor for filling soil and pile driving requires bare soil before starting work
  • Before surveying or subdividing — The land officer must be able to access the marker
  • Before announcing for sale or rent — Buyers can see the actual size and condition, making it easier to decide
  • Abandoned land — According to the Land and Building Tax Act B.E. 2562, land assessed as abandoned or vacant is taxed at a higher rate than land that is in use. Many owners therefore clear the land to put it to use. You should inquire about the conditions with the Subdistrict Administrative Organization (SAO) or the municipality in the area beforehand.
  • A dry season when the grass is withered — Reduce the risk of grass fires, snakes, poisonous animals, and illegal dumping

4.excerpt_en: The residential solar program lets homeowners install rooftop panels for self-use and sell surplus power back to the utility at 2.20 THB per unit under a 10-year contract. 4.meta_description_en: Residential solar program 2026 summary — sell power at 2.20 THB/unit for 10 years. Conditions, documents, and MEA/PEA registration steps. Ask BOA-Buildtech.
4.body_en:
Summarize quickly

  • Purchase rate: 2.20 Baht/unit Duration 10 years
  • Cannot be sold more than 5 kW (AC) per meter · Total purchase target 500 MW
  • Open for requests From July 1, 2026 onwards Until the quota is full (First come, First served)
  • Supply power to the system (SCOD) By 2027
  • Submit where: Bangkok/Nonthaburi/Samut Prakan → MEA's My Energy | Other provinces include Pathum Thani → PPIM of EA

What is the community solar cells project, and how is it different in the year 2026 compared to before?

The community solar cell project is a program for purchasing electricity from solar power systems installed on residential rooftops, focusing on homeowners to primarily 'generate electricity for their own use' (Self Consumption), and then sell only the excess electricity that flows back into the grid to the electricity distribution company, rather than installing it to sell all the electricity.

The 2026 round occurred after the ERC passed a resolution in its 25/2569 meeting on June 24, 2026, approving the announcement to invite applications for the purchase of electricity from rooftop solar power projects for the residential sector in 2026. The point that clearly differs from the previous round is The quota size has increased significantly to 500 megawatts And the electricity sales cap is set at 5 kilowatts (AC) per meter, with a clear timeframe for feeding electricity into the system by 2027.

What needs to be clearly understood from the beginning: this project uses a separated billing mechanism — the electricity we buy from the power authority is charged at the regular rate, while the electricity we sell back is calculated at 2.20 baht per unit. It is not a direct unit-offset like Net Metering. Therefore, most of the actual savings come from 'using self-generated electricity during the daytime,' not from selling electricity.

What are the conditions for solar cells for the public in 2026?

The main conditions are that you must be a Type 1 electricity user, a residential household, offering to sell no more than 5 kilowatts (AC) per meter at a rate of 2.20 baht per unit, with a 10-year contract. Homeowners must invest in the installation costs entirely by themselves. Applications will be considered on a first-come, first-served basis until the target of 500 megawatts is reached, and electricity must be fed into the commercial system by 2027.

ConditionDetails as announced
Eligible personIndividual, Type 1 electricity user, residential house
Offered QuantityNo more than 5 kilowatts (AC) per electricity purchase meter
Purchase rate2.20 baht/unit (kWh)
Contract duration10 years
Total purchase targetNo more than 500 megawatts (AC) for the entire area of both PEA and MEA combined
Method of considerationFirst come, first served. Based on the date and time when the documents are completely submitted.
Announcement of resultsWithin 30 days from the date of submitting a complete application
Sign the contractWithin 30 days from the date of announcement of the list, otherwise the request is canceled.
System Connection Date (SCOD)By 2027
InvestorThe homeowner invested in the entire power generation system by themselves.

The point that people most often misunderstand: A 5 kW ceiling does not mean that installation over 5 kW is prohibited, but it means that the maximum electricity power that can be fed back to the utility is no more than 5 kW (AC) per meter. Houses that use a lot of electricity during the day can still install a larger size for their own use, but the system and reverse-flow control equipment must be designed according to the local utility's connection requirements.

Who can apply for solar cells for the public sector, and who cannot?

Applications are only available for Type 1 electricity users, residential households, where the name on the electricity bill, the house number of installation, and the type of user match the applicant's information. Small business meters, commercial buildings, rental dormitories, or factories do not meet the conditions of this project.

Check 4 points before submitting

  1. Open the electricity bill to check whether the type of electricity user is 'Type 1 Residential'.
  2. Does the name of the meter owner match the applicant? If not, a power of attorney is required.
  3. The attached electricity bill must be current (should not be older than 3 months)
  4. If the information in the system is still incorrect, you must contact the local electricity office to have it corrected. Before Submit to join the project

Item 4 is the reason why many requests end up wasted, because the project uses a first-come, first-served principle.

Where can the public register for solar cells? Houses in Pathum Thani and Nonthaburi are on different systems.

The registration channel depends on which electric utility area the house is in. Electricity users in Bangkok, Nonthaburi, and Samut Prakan submit through the My Energy system of the Metropolitan Electricity Authority (MEA). myenergy.mea.or.th As for electricity users in other provinces across the country, including Pathum Thani, they submit through the PPIM system of the Provincial Electricity Authority (PEA) at ppim.pea.co.th

The house is atThe electricity authority in chargeApplication submission system
Nonthaburi (Pak Kret, Bang Bua Thong, Sai Noi, etc.)Metropolitan Electricity Authority (MEA)My Energy — myenergy.mea.or.th
Bangkok, Samut PrakanMetropolitan Electricity Authority (MEA)My Energy — myenergy.mea.or.th
Pathum Thani (Rangsit Lam Luk Ka Thanyaburi Khlong Luang Lat Lum Kaeo Sam Khok)Provincial Electricity Authority (PEA)PPIM — ppim.pea.co.th
Other provinces across the countryProvincial Electricity Authority (PEA)PPIM — ppim.pea.co.th

For houses in the Rangsit–Lam Luk Ka–Pak Kret area, you need to check the correct electricity authority zone, because submitting to the wrong system means wasting time waiting and having to submit again according to the new queue.

How many steps are there to apply online for solar cells for the public?

Online application starts by registering a user account in the electricity authority system, filling out the electricity sales request form, and uploading documents. Wait for the decision within 30 days, pay the system connection fee and sign the contract within 30 days after the result is announced. Then install the system, request a network connection, change the meter, and supply electricity to the system within the SCOD deadline.

Procedures according to the PPIM system of PEA (Pathum Thani area and other provinces)

  1. Register a user account in the PPIM system (select the type 'General public')
  2. Log in and select the solar power generation project installed on rooftops for the public sector (applications submitted from 2026)
  3. Select the CA number of the meter to be installed, fill out the application form, and upload all the required attachments.
  4. PEA reviews the documents and the technical readiness of the distribution system and then notifies the results by email.
  5. Announcement of the list of applicants who pass the selection in the system within 30 days from the date the application is complete.
  6. Selected candidates shall pay the network connection fee and submit the original documents for contract signing within 30 days.
  7. Sign a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with the regional electricity authority, with the SCOD scheduled within 2027
  8. Install the system according to the submitted specification and then submit a request to connect to the power grid.
  9. Notify the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) of energy business operations that are exempt from requiring a license.
  10. The electricity authority inspected the system, replaced the meter, and tested the connection for the first time (First Synchronization)
  11. Supply power to the commercial system (COD) no later than the SCOD specified in the contract

Note from the site: The PPIM system will set the request status to 'Awaiting Document Upload' if the documents are incomplete (request numbers starting with D), which Not yet considered a complete submission You must upload everything completely until the status changes to 'Waiting for request review' before the queue order will actually start counting.

What documents and expenses need to be prepared?

The main documents that need to be prepared are the ID card, a copy of the household registration of the house where the installation will take place, an electricity bill not older than 3 months, the installation plan and electrical system diagram (Single Line Diagram), information about the equipment used, and a power of attorney in case the applicant is not the meter owner.

Regarding the expenses on the electricity side, PEA has set the fee for the system connection inspection at 2,000 baht excluding tax or 2,140 baht including 7% value-added tax Charged after the request has been approved. All equipment and system installation costs are the responsibility of the homeowner.

Technical requirements that are often overlooked

  • The inverter used must be registered with the Electricity Authority — on the PEA side, the list can be checked at smartlist.pea.co.th/products
  • The MEA side requires that the equipment controlling the reverse flow of electricity into the system (Export Limiting Device: EXL) must be tested by the MEA.
  • The installation of an energy storage system (BESS) together with rooftop solar in this project No restrictions As notified by the ERC, it must be carried out in accordance with the engineering standards of the contracted distribution electricity authority.

Choosing the wrong model of equipment from the day of purchase is equivalent to failing, or you have to replace the entire inverter set. The installer should verify the list of equipment with the electricity authority's registry. Before Sign quotation

Do I need to get permission to modify the building to install solar cells on the roof?

According to the amendment of the ministerial regulations issued under the Building Control Act B.E. 2522, which the Cabinet approved in principle on May 6, 2025, the installation of solar panels on the rooftop of a building with a total weight in any particular area No more than 20 kilograms per square meter is not considered a building modification. Therefore, there is no need to apply for a building modification permit (Form A.1)

But 'no need to ask for permission' does not equal 'no need to check the structure' — old houses, thin metal sheet roofs, or wooden roof frames still need to have their actual load-bearing capacity assessed before installation, and the installation must not violate local ordinances or the regulations of the housing project.

Selling electricity at 2.20 baht per unit, is it worth it and what size should be installed?

The value of this project comes from 'using self-generated electricity during the daytime' rather than income from selling electricity, because the purchase rate of 2.20 baht per unit is lower than the electricity rate we buy from the electricity authority. The most worthwhile houses are those with people at home during the day and regularly using the air conditioner during the daytime.

Practical system sizing design principles

  1. Look at the electricity usage from the bill over the past 6–12 months and then assess the proportion of electricity used between 09:00–16:00.
  2. Design the system size to align with the use of daylight as the primary source, not based on the maximum number of panels the roof can accommodate.
  3. Check the usable roof area after accounting for shadows, ventilation stacks, and panel orientation
  4. Set the grid feed-in power not to exceed 5 kW (AC) according to the project conditions
  5. Evaluate the breakeven point from the actual quotation, not from the average figures in the advertisement.

If you want the technician team to assess the roof and design the system size, you can see the details on the page Install solar cells electrical system work BOA-Buildtech

Why do community solar cell projects mainly need a team that works on electrical systems?

Because the steps that cause the application to be delayed or rejected are mostly not related to solar panels, but to electrical documents, such as a Single Line Diagram that does not match the installed equipment, inverters not registered with the electricity authority, or anti-islanding protection systems that do not meet the connection requirements.

BOA-Buildtech works on electrical systems and civil engineering in the areas of Pathum Thani, Nonthaburi, Bangkok, and surrounding regions, covering everything from roof structure inspection and electrical system installation to coordinating documents with the local electricity authority, so homeowners do not have to handle coordination through multiple channels themselves.

Summary and next steps

The 2569 (2026) solar cells project for the public sector will accept applications starting from July 1, 2569, on a first-come, first-served basis until the target of 500 megawatts is reached. Electricity can be sold up to 5 kW (AC) per meter at a rate of 2.20 baht per unit for 10 years, and electricity must be fed into the system by 2027.

Why does land filling in Bang Kruai have different costs from other places?

Many plots of land in Bang Kruai are old garden plots along the canal on the west side of the Chao Phraya River. There are four specific factors that make the budget for fill soil different from ordinary vacant land.

garden furrows and furrow bottom lanes

In the garden, there are water channels alternating with earthen embankments. Before filling, the water must be pumped out, and usually the mud at the bottom of the channels has to be dredged first. If the mud is covered with soil, the ground will later subside into holes. The channels also increase the amount of soil needed. For example, if the channels occupy 40% of the plot (640 square meters) and are 1.5 meters deep, an additional 960 cubic meters of soil will be needed before starting to measure the desired fill height.

Soft clay and settlement

The original soil in this zone is soft clay, the same type as in Bangkok. The thicker the fill, the more the underlying soil is continuously compressed over many years. Therefore, it is necessary to fill and compact in layers, and allow time for the soil to settle before construction. Narrow alley and vehicle restrictions

The size of vehicles that can access the site directly determines the transportation costs (see the table above). Some plots require the construction of temporary roads.

Water level and road level

Bang Kruai is a low-lying area that used to experience severe flooding. Choosing the fill height therefore requires considering the level of the road in front of the house, the land level of neighboring properties, and the flood marks from previous floods in the area.

Small-area or thin-layer work often has a higher cost per cubic meter than large filling projects because the cost of bringing machinery in and out of the site is almost the same, but it is divided by a smaller amount of soil. Narrow sections force the use of small vehicles, so the per-cubic-meter price of small projects should not be directly multiplied for a 1-rai project.

How high should the land filling be, and what type of soil should be used?

The appropriate height is 'slightly higher than the road level in front of the land and above the flood level that has occurred in the area.' It is not necessary to fill to the highest possible level within the budget, because every additional meter of height requires about 1,900–2,100 cubic meters of soil per rai and increases the weight pressing down on the soft soil below.

Choose the height according to usage

  • Land held or waiting to be sold: Fill it to prevent water pooling and level it with the road. Mostly around 0.5–1 meter.
  • Build a residential house: Fill it slightly higher than the road, then have the engineer determine the floor level again.
  • Warehouse or parking lot: It needs to be compacted more tightly and may be covered on the surface with laterite. The density specifications should be discussed before setting the budget.

  1. Inspect the site and measure the level: Measure the land level in comparison with the road and neighboring plots, check garden furrows, lanes, and vehicle entrances
  2. Extract soil quantities and issue a quotation: Specify the number of queues, type of soil, and clearly state the items included or not included.

  4. Build earthen embankments/soil edges and drainage paths: Prevent soil from sliding into the neighbor's property or into the canal
  5. Pile soil and spread it into layers: Each layer is about 30–50 cm, then compact each layer.

Common mistakes encountered when landfilling

  • Covering mud or weeds without removing them: The ground will sink into a depression afterward.
  • Compare quotations from different bases: One thinks each trip, another thinks in queue; the smaller number may get less soil.
  • Did not make a drainage system: Rainwater flows down to the neighbor, becoming a dispute
  • Build a house immediately after land filling: The ground around the house has sunk, the pipes are broken, the walkway is cracked

Do I need permission to fill 1 rai of land?

For 1 rai of land (1,600 sq.m.), generally, there is no need to notify the local authorities about soil filling. However, there are still legal obligations under Section 26 of the Excavation and Soil Filling Act B.E. 2543 (2000). Soil filling higher than neighboring land and covering an area not exceeding 2,000 sq.m. must ensure proper drainage to avoid causing inconvenience to neighbors. For land filling covering an area over 2,000 sq.m. or exceeding the criteria announced by the local authorities, it must be reported to the local officer.

The precaution is that local officials can announce the area criteria by themselves, but it must not exceed 2,000 sq.m. Before starting the work, you should check with the municipality or subdistrict administrative organization (SAO) where the land is located to see if there is a smaller area criteria announced in that zone.

This article is general information and is not legal advice. For specific cases, you should check directly with local authorities.

70.question_en: Can you replace only broken glass without changing the existing frame?

71.question_en: Aluminum or uPVC — which is better?
71.answer_en: Aluminum suits large leaves and thinner frames because it is stronger at the same thickness and offers more colors. uPVC insulates heat and sound better at similar sizes, but large leaves need internal steel and thicker frames. 73.question_en: How do aluminum awnings differ from metal-sheet awnings?
73.answer_en: Aluminum does not rust and is lighter, so it suits limited wall capacity and high-humidity areas. Metal sheet costs less per square meter and covers large areas more economically. Both use similar framing; the main differences are cladding material, lifespan, and budget.

74.question_en: Can an awning be fixed to a masonry wall?
74.answer_en: Usually yes, but the wall must be checked first. Clay brick and concrete block take anchors differently. 75.question_en: How many years does an aluminum awning last?
75.answer_en: Lifespan has three parts: the aluminum frame (longest, non-rusting), the coated finish (fades with direct sun), and silicone plus fixings (need attention first). Joints and fixings usually age before the panels themselves.

76.question_en: Does an awning extension need a permit?
