91.question_en: How many cubic meters of soil to fill 1 rai?
91.answer_en: One rai equals 1,600 square meters. Filling 1 meter high needs 1,600 compacted cubic meters and about 2,000 loose cubic meters ordered to allow 20–25% compaction settlement. Filling 50 cm needs 800 compacted or about 1,000 loose cubic meters.

92.question_en: What is the difference between loose and compacted cubic meters?
92.answer_en: Loose cubic meters are soil volume on the truck bed. Compacted cubic meters are the volume remaining in the plot after compaction. Soil settles about 15–25% between those stages. Before comparing quotes, always ask whether the price is loose or compacted — 350 THB per loose cubic meter is roughly 440 THB per compacted cubic meter. 93.question_en: How high should land be filled in Rangsit, Thanyaburi, and Lam Luk Ka?
93.answer_en: There is no single number for every plot. It comes from three values: level relative to the public road, highest flood level known in that soi, and allowance for future settlement. Adjacent plots can differ by 30–40 cm if they sit on different canal or dyke sides. We measure and calculate free at survey.

94.question_en: Must land filling be notified to the local authority?
94.answer_en: If the fill area exceeds 2,000 square meters (about 1 rai 1 ngan), you must notify the local authority before starting under the Excavation and Land Filling Act B.E. 2543 (2000), and start only after receiving the acknowledgment. Below that threshold notification is not required, but adequate drainage must still protect neighboring land. Localities may set a lower area threshold.

95.question_en: Will filled land settle? Can you build immediately or must you wait?
95.answer_en: Some settlement always occurs because soft clay layers about 10–18 m deep compress under fill load. What the contractor controls is settlement of the fill itself, prevented by layered compaction to standard. Piled buildings can start once compaction passes criteria. Works sitting directly on fill — ground-bearing slabs, internal roads, or fences — should wait through at least one rainy season.

96.question_en: How do you choose a land-filling contractor to avoid later problems?
96.answer_en: Ask for three things before signing: (1) whether the contract prices loose or compacted cubic meters; (2) compaction specs and verification method (layer thickness and density testing); (3) clear warranty scope of what is and is not covered. Contractors who cannot answer these three are often the source of volume and settlement disputes.

195.question_en: How much does a 5 kW home solar installation cost?
195.answer_en: On-Grid 5 kW 1-phase is 159,850 THB incl. VAT; 3-phase is 177,100 THB incl. VAT. Hybrid 5 kW 1-phase without battery is 154,100 THB; with a 10 kWh battery it is 182,850 THB. All use Solis inverters and include VAT.

196.question_en: How much does a 3 kW solar installation cost?
196.answer_en: 3 kW 1-phase is 142,600 THB incl. VAT for both On-Grid and Hybrid without battery. Suitable for homes using about 400–600 units/month or bills around 2,500–4,000 THB/month, cutting bills by roughly 1,400–1,800 THB/month.

197.question_en: How much tax deduction can solar installation claim?
197.answer_en: BOA-Buildtech issues an E-TAX Invoice on every job for residential solar installation tax deduction up to 200,000 THB under Revenue Department rules. You need the E-TAX Invoice plus house-registration address for e-Filing in the tax year of payment. Check the latest Revenue Department conditions before deciding.

198.question_en: How many years is the warranty, and what does it cover?
198.answer_en: Solar panels 30 years, Solis inverter 10 years, and battery 10 years, with professional after-sales support. The 30-year panel warranty exceeds the typical market standard of about 25 years.

199.question_en: On-Grid or Hybrid — which home solar system is better?
199.answer_en: Homes with heavy daytime use and existing utility power get the best value from On-Grid (no battery cost). Hybrid suits heavy nighttime use, critical loads that cannot stop, or frequent outages — at higher cost and longer payback.

200.question_en: What permits are needed for solar installation?
200.answer_en: Grid-tied systems need interconnection approval from MEA (Bangkok, Nonthaburi, Samut Prakan) or PEA (Pathum Thani and other provinces), plus local building-alteration notice and ERC registration. We handle all of this; the owner prepares ID copy, house registration, electricity bill, and land title documents.

201.question_en: How many days does installation take?
201.answer_en: Rooftop installation for a typical home takes 2–4 days, but the full process from contract to utility meter change and energization is about 30–60 days. Most time is utility approval; we track status and update you periodically.

202.question_en: Where do you install solar cells?
202.answer_en: Pathum Thani, Nonthaburi, all Bangkok districts, and surrounding provinces including Samut Prakan and Nakhon Pathom. Site survey and quotation are free in every service area.

203.question_en: What is the 2026 residential solar buyback rate, and for how many years?
203.answer_en: Surplus power is bought at 2.20 THB per unit for 10 years from commercial operation, capped at 5 kW (AC) per meter. Import and export are billed separately — not simple net metering of units.

204.question_en: Until when can I apply for the residential solar program?
204.answer_en: Utilities open applications from 1 July 2026 until the 500 MW national quota is filled, first-come first-served — no fixed closing date. Prepare documents and apply early. Systems must energize by 2027.

205.question_en: Which website is used for residential solar online registration?
205.answer_en: Customers in Bangkok, Nonthaburi, and Samut Prakan apply via MEA My Energy at myenergy.mea.or.th. Other provinces including Pathum Thani use PEA PPIM at ppim.pea.co.th. Applying in the wrong system means the request will not be considered.

206.question_en: What fees does the utility charge for joining the program?
206.answer_en: PEA charges a 2,000 THB interconnection review fee excluding VAT (2,140 THB incl. VAT), billed after the application is approved. All generation equipment and installation costs are paid by the homeowner.

207.question_en: Can I install more than 5 kW?
207.answer_en: Yes. The 5 kW (AC) cap is the maximum export per meter, not the maximum install size. Homes with heavy daytime use can install larger systems for self-use but must control export per utility interconnection rules.

208.question_en: Does rooftop solar require a building-alteration permit?
208.answer_en: Under the amended ministerial regulation, rooftop PV with total weight not exceeding 20 kg per square meter is not considered a building alteration, so an alteration permit (A.1) is not required. Still have a professional check roof structure capacity and local ordinances before installing.

209.question_en: What is the starting price for aluminum works, and how is it calculated?
209.answer_en: Aluminum doors and windows start around 3,500–8,500 THB/sq.m. (excluding installation labor), based on actual glass area, leaf type, profile, and glass type — see the price table above for ranges. Confirmed prices appear only in the quotation after site measure.

210.question_en: Is there a minimum job size? Do you take small jobs?
210.answer_en: No minimum for residential work such as replacing 1–2 leaves or fitting insect screens. Small jobs follow crew scheduling. Project or long-distance work may have BOQ minimums disclosed at quoting.

211.question_en: How many days from site measure to finished installation?
211.answer_en: Typical homes take about 12–21 business days from measure appointment to finished install. Rush jobs or large projects get a separate schedule in the quotation.

212.question_en: How many years is aluminum work warranted, and what is covered?
212.answer_en: Aluminum installation is warranted 1 year for installation defects, sealant leaks, and hardware we installed. Impact-broken glass, misuse, or third-party modification after handover are excluded.

213.question_en: Do you work outside Bangkok? Is there a travel surcharge?
213.answer_en: We work nationwide. Bangkok and surrounding provinces get free site measure. Other provinces may have a survey travel fee, which can be credited against the job if you hire us.

214.question_en: Aluminum or uPVC — which should I choose?
214.answer_en: Aluminum handles sun and rain well and suits large leaves, at higher price. uPVC is lighter, better insulated, and more economical, but very wide leaves may deflect. Choose by budget, opening size, and sun exposure — we advise after seeing the site.

215.question_en: How do bored piles differ from driven piles?
215.answer_en: Bored piles are cast in a hole drilled on site — low vibration and high capacity. Driven piles are factory-made and driven into the ground — faster and more economical on open sites, but vibration may affect neighboring buildings. Choice depends on building load, soil strata, and surroundings.

216.question_en: Which piles work for factory extensions without stopping the production line?
216.answer_en: Live-plant extensions often use micropiles or dry-process bored piles because equipment is small, vibration is low, and work can stay close to existing structure. Coordinate timing with production and check underground utilities before starting.

217.question_en: Can micropiles be used for new buildings?
217.answer_en: Yes if the engineer sizes enough piles for the building load. Micropiles carry less per pile than large bored or driven piles, so more piles per footing are common. For new buildings with crane access, other systems are often more economical.

218.question_en: Can hexagonal piles be used for house foundations?
218.answer_en: Not recommended for primary house structure. Hexagonal piles suit light loads such as fences, gazebos, or parking yards. For extensions attached to the house, an engineer should assess differential settlement versus the existing building.

219.question_en: Is a soil boring report required before piling?
219.answer_en: For factories and large buildings, yes — soil investigation guides pile length and count, reducing settlement risk and unnecessary piles. Small jobs may use local reference data at the engineer’s judgment.

220.question_en: How much does I-pile driving cost?
220.answer_en: I-pile pricing has two parts: pile units at 143–347 THB per meter by size and grade, and driving — 1–99 piles as a lump sum from 26,400–33,000 THB; over 100 piles at 633–1,100 THB per pile. Figures assume 2 spliced sections, exclude VAT, and move with material and fuel prices.

221.question_en: How many days does a project piling job take?
221.answer_en: Duration depends on pile system, pile count, and site conditions, excluding testing and waiting for concrete to reach design strength. The team states the schedule in the work plan after site survey.

222.question_en: How much does house demolition cost?
222.answer_en: Single-storey detached houses roughly 40,000–120,000 THB/building; two-storey about 80,000–220,000 THB/building; row houses and townhouses 350–800 THB/sq.m. Actual price depends on size and structure, soi width, haul distance, and scrap credit. Send site photos via LINE for a free preliminary range.

223.question_en: Does house demolition require a permit?
223.answer_en: Yes — notify or apply to the local authority when Building Control Act Section 22 applies: buildings over 15 m within less than their height of another building or public land, or buildings within 2 m of another building or public land — covering almost all row houses and townhouses. Check with the district office, municipality, or Subdistrict Administrative Organization before starting.

224.question_en: How many days does house demolition take?
224.answer_en: Single-storey detached homes typically 3–7 days for demolition and hauling; two-storey about 7–14 days. Row houses and townhouses may take longer due to party-wall shoring and staged strip-out. This excludes permit processing — allow about 1–1.5 months before the start date.

225.question_en: Is free house or building demolition real?
225.answer_en: Sometimes — when salvage value (old timber, steel frames, metal roofing) fully offsets labor, equipment, and hauling. Common for old wooden houses or steel-frame buildings. Concrete houses yield little scrap, so a fee is usual. BOA-Buildtech shows scrap credits as separate quotation lines.

226.question_en: Will row-house demolition affect neighboring homes?
226.answer_en: It can if the party wall is not shored first. We survey and photograph neighboring conditions before work, shore the party wall, cut structure in stages instead of pushing the whole building over, hang dust sheets, and wet-down dust during demolition to reduce cracking risk and neighbor disputes.

227.question_en: After demolition, what must be done before building a new house?
227.answer_en: Notify the local registrar within 15 days after demolition, and check whether old piles or footings must be extracted before fill and new piles. BOA-Buildtech can continue with the same team — clearing, fill, compaction, and foundation piles — so you do not need multiple contractors.

228.question_en: Do row house / townhouse demolitions need a permit?
228.answer_en: Almost always, because they sit within 2 m of other buildings or public land under Building Control Act Section 22. Local authorities have 45 days to decide. BOA-Buildtech checks at survey and can file Form Khor.1 for the owner in our service districts.

229.question_en: How much does row-house demolition cost per square meter?
229.answer_en: About 350–800 THB per square meter for residential work. Price rises with storeys, party-wall length to shore, and sois that large trucks cannot enter. Permit fees are a separate line. Confirmed after site survey. Call 061-743-9900 for a free assessment.

230.answer_en: Usually not — row houses are mostly concrete, and recovered steel rarely covers labor, shoring, and hauling out of a soi. Recoverable rebar, steel doors, window bars, and metal roofing are valued and credited clearly in the quotation.

231.question_en: If a neighboring house cracks after demolishing an attached house, who is responsible?
231.answer_en: The contractor who caused the damage must repair or compensate. BOA-Buildtech photo-records neighboring conditions with the owner before work, shores party walls, and controls dust per contract. New cracks proven from our demolition are inspected and repaired by us.

232.question_en: If the soi is too narrow for a backhoe, can a row house still be demolished?
232.answer_en: Yes, using smaller machines or manual strip-out and multiple 6-wheel haul trips. Days and price per square meter are higher than jobs with large-machine access. Send photos of the soi entrance and turning space at assessment so we can say early how far we can reach.

233.question_en: After demolishing a row house, who cares for the newly exposed neighbor wall?
233.answer_en: Agree this clearly in the contract before starting — a wall that was once interior will face sun and rain for the first time. BOA-Buildtech offers neighbor-side wall finishing as a separate quotation line (e.g. plaster and waterproofing, or cladding) to avoid later disputes.

234.question_en: How many days to clear 1 rai of land?
234.answer_en: A 1-rai plot with only grass and shrubs typically takes 1–2 working days. Large trees, stumps, or heavy building debris may take 3–7+ days. Actual time depends on vegetation density, haul trips, and soil conditions. The quotation always states a time frame.

235.question_en: Does land clearing include hauling timber and waste off site?
235.answer_en: It depends on what the quotation specifies. Some contractors only cut and pile on site. BOA-Buildtech itemizes “haul debris off site” as clear truck-trip counts so owners can choose full removal or keep some timber for their own use.

236.question_en: Do I need a permit to cut trees on my own land?
236.answer_en: Generally no — after the 2019 Forest Act amendment, trees on privately titled land are no longer reserved timber. Housing estates still need juristic-person approval before bringing machines in, and if buildings are also demolished, ask the district office or municipality about demolition notice.

237.question_en: After clearing, must fill start immediately?
237.answer_en: Not on every plot. If existing level is not below the road or neighbors and water does not pond, clearing plus grading may be enough. Many Pathum Thani–Nonthaburi plots sit below road level — measure after clearing, then decide fill height.

238.question_en: Do you clear land during the rainy season?
238.answer_en: Yes, but each plot must be assessed — saturated clay can bog excavators and damage the surface, so some jobs should wait until rain pauses. Firm ground or good access can proceed normally. We disclose risks before agreeing a start date.

239.question_en: What information is needed for a land-clearing quotation?
239.answer_en: Provide plot coordinates or a Google Maps pin, titled area, multiple photos or videos of current condition, and intended use (house, warehouse, or sale). This supports a close preliminary estimate before a real site survey.

245.question_en: How much does a steel pile cost each?
245.answer_en: Per the Budget Bureau Thai Innovation Account, KEMREX FS helical steel piles 2 m long start at 6,100 THB each; the 6 m model is 85,000 THB each. Prices include VAT but exclude transport and installation. Actual cost depends on model and pile count designed by the engineer.

246.question_en: How many tons can a steel pile carry?
246.answer_en: ASTM tests show 2 m models with ultimate point compression of 7.44–14.66 tons, and FS355 6 m models up to 80 tons. Design values divide by a Safety Factor of 2–4 set by the engineer for the soil strata, so they are lower than these figures.

247.answer_en: U.S. National Bureau of Standards studies found no significant corrosion on steel piles in undisturbed soil below the water table over 7–40 years. Risk is higher in fill layers. Steel piles sold in Thailand are therefore hot-dip galvanized at least 100 micrometers thick.

248.question_en: How do helical steel piles differ from micropiles?
248.answer_en: Helical steel piles are screwed into the ground and carry load on the helical flights. International micropiles are grouted drilled piles under about 300 mm with steel bar or casing. Thai concrete micropiles are often driven or jacked prefabricated sections about 1.5 m long.

249.question_en: How should you choose a steel pile company?
249.answer_en: Choose a company whose engineer designs from real soil boring data, uses hot-dip galvanized piles with ASTM test results, records final torque on every pile, and separates pile, transport, and installation prices in the quotation.

250.question_en: Are steel piles a good choice, and for which jobs?
250.answer_en: Steel piles suit extensions and light structures in tight sites where noise, dust, and vibration must stay low. They are a poor fit for rocky ground or shallow rock, and an engineer must always design from real soil data.

251.question_en: How many cubic meters of soil to fill 1 rai?
251.answer_en: Filling 1 rai to 1 m needs 1,600 net cubic meters but about 1,920–2,080 ordered because soil settles 20–30% after compaction. At 2 m height, net is 3,200 cubic meters and ordered about 3,840–4,160. Plots with old orchard ditches or ponds need extra ditch volume.

252.question_en: How many truck trips to fill 1 rai?
252.answer_en: At 1 m height, a 6-wheel truck at ~3 cu.m. per trip needs about 640–700 trips, or a 10-wheel about 130–175 trips. At 2 m height, about 1,280–1,390 six-wheel trips. Actual counts depend on bed size and whether 10-wheel trucks can enter — many Bang Kruai sois allow only 6-wheel access.

253.question_en: Does filling 1 rai require a permit?
253.answer_en: One rai (1,600 sq.m.) is under 2,000 sq.m., so notification under the Excavation and Land Filling Act B.E. 2543 (2000) is generally not required. Drainage must still protect neighbors, and localities may set a lower threshold — ask the municipality or Subdistrict Administrative Organization before starting.

254.question_en: Can you build a house right after filling?
254.answer_en: Not immediately — especially in Bang Kruai soft clay. Fill continues to settle; compact in layers and allow at least 3–6 months or one rainy season. Houses need engineer-designed piles, and ground floors should be beam-supported slabs, not ground-bearing slabs.

255.question_en: Can land be filled in the rainy season?
255.answer_en: Possible but not recommended — wet soil will not compact well, trucks bog down, and ditch pumping increases, slowing work and raising cost. The best Nonthaburi window is the dry season around November–April. If rain-season fill is necessary, choose free-draining soil and plan truck access carefully.

256.question_en: Why do land-filling prices differ so much between contractors?
256.answer_en: Bases differ — some price per truck trip, some per loose cubic meter, some per compacted cubic meter, and some quotes omit grading, compaction, pumping, or ditch sludge removal. Before comparing, ask every contractor to state soil volume in cubic meters, soil type, and what is included or excluded.

263.question_en: How much does shop design cost?
263.answer_en: Shop design is typically about 800–2,000 THB per square meter depending on area, 2D/3D detail, and revision rounds. Fit-out installation starts around 8,000–25,000 THB per square meter for retail and higher for cafés or restaurants with kitchen works. BOA-Buildtech surveys and estimates free. Call 061-743-9900.

264.question_en: How many days does shop design take?
264.answer_en: After site survey, layout and mood board take about 5–10 business days; 3D and material schedules another 7–14 business days, depending on shop size and owner confirmation speed. Small-to-mid fit-out construction usually takes 3–6 weeks after contract and materials are ready.

265.question_en: Design only, or through to installation?
265.answer_en: BOA-Buildtech offers design-only or design-plus fit-out in one team — floors, walls, ceilings, built-ins, aluminum-glass, and electrical — reducing multi-contractor coordination and keeping the budget clearer.

266.question_en: What should I know about designing a shop in a mall?
266.answer_en: Mall shops must follow the tenant manual — working hours, noise, dust, power/water points, fire systems, and storefront material standards. Request the rules file before design to avoid redraws and site rework. Quotations should allow about 10–15% contingency for extra mall-required work.

267.question_en: What should I prepare before design starts?
267.answer_en: Prepare a floor plan or approximate size, rough budget, preferred style, reference brands, main products/menu, key selling points, and the tenant manual if in a mall. Send site photos via LINE — we reply with budget range and approach within 1 business day.

268.answer_en: BOA-Buildtech designs and fits out shops in Bangkok, Nonthaburi, Pathum Thani, Samut Prakan, Samut Sakhon, and Nakhon Pathom. The office is in Thanyaburi, Pathum Thani, for quick surveys in Rangsit, Bangkok, and surrounding provinces.

281.question_en: How much does construction waste hauling cost per trip?
281.answer_en: 6-wheel 3 cu.m. from 800 THB/trip, or 1,400 THB/trip with labor. 6-wheel 7 cu.m. from 1,400 THB/trip, or 2,000 THB/trip with labor. Out-of-province runs are 32 THB/km (3 cu.m.) and 35 THB/km (7 cu.m.). Prices adjust with fuel. Call 061-743-9900 to confirm the day rate.

282.question_en: Where can construction waste be dumped? Is it illegal otherwise?
282.answer_en: Waste must go to locally approved construction-debris tips. Dumping roadside, on vacant land, or into waterways is illegal. BOA-Buildtech lists the tip and tip fees in the quotation and does not dump outside approved sites.

283.question_en: Can concrete, brick, timber, and asbestos tiles be hauled together?
283.answer_en: Concrete, brick, general tile, and most timber can usually share a load if the tip accepts them. Asbestos cement sheets must be separated and handled differently — never smashed into general debris. Tell us when sending assessment photos so we plan the correct method.

284.question_en: If the soi is too narrow for a 6-wheel truck, can waste still be hauled?
284.answer_en: Yes — use pickups or small trucks for multiple trips, or stage at the soi mouth then load a larger truck. Trip count and price per trip are higher than jobs with large-truck access. Send photos of the entrance and turning space at assessment.

285.question_en: Can I hire hauling only, without demolition or clearing?
285.answer_en: Yes. This page is debris hauling only — ideal when piles are already ready. Brush and tree cutting is under land clearing; post-demolition clearing is under the post-demolition clearing page.

286.question_en: Where do you haul construction waste?
286.answer_en: BOA-Buildtech works in Bangkok, Nonthaburi, Pathum Thani, Samut Prakan, and nearby provinces. Survey or photo assessment via LINE is free in our service area. Book at 061-743-9900.

287.answer_en: Yes. BOA-Buildtech is a used air conditioner buyer based in Pathum Thani, serving Pathum Thani, Nonthaburi, and northern Bangkok — including Rangsit, Lam Luk Ka, Pak Kret, Bang Bua Thong, Don Mueang, and Sai Mai. Send AC photos with your area via LINE for a quote and removal booking.

288.question_en: How much do you pay for used air conditioners?
288.answer_en: Complete used sets are bought for 700–5,400 THB by BTU size and coil material — e.g. 12,000 BTU copper coil 1,700 THB and 18,000 BTU copper coil 2,500 THB. Aluminium coils pay less; inverter units are priced at 60% of the standard rate.

289.question_en: Do you buy broken used air conditioners?
289.answer_en: Yes. Broken units with main parts intact pay the same table rates because we price copper, aluminium, steel, and the compressor — not cooling performance. If the compressor was removed or the coil cut, the price drops for missing parts and is always stated before removal.

290.question_en: Can older vintage air conditioners still be sold?
290.answer_en: Yes — and they often pay well because older units usually have copper coils and are not inverters, so they land in the highest table column. If the spec label is faded, photograph the whole unit and room size; the technician can estimate BTU.

291.question_en: How much do you pay for used compressors?
291.answer_en: Removed compressors are bought by size because the copper windings and steel shell still have value. Photograph the label on the compressor and send it via LINE for a quote. If the compressor is still on the unit, selling the full set usually pays more than parting it out.

292.question_en: Can flood-damaged air conditioners be sold?
292.answer_en: Yes. Even when a submerged compressor is unusable, copper, aluminium, and steel still have value. BOA-Buildtech buys by remaining parts. If the coil is heavily corroded, send photos via LINE and we will quote before booking removal.

293.question_en: Can I sell the old AC and install a new one together?
293.answer_en: Yes — remove and buy back the old unit at table rates, then install the new one in one appointment. The technician checks whether existing wiring and breakers support the new unit, which cuts travel cost and avoids taking two days off.
